findings.title: isinstance guard makes kill()/terminate() dead code for spawn processes, so hung flushers are never killed
findings.body: The check `isinstance(process, multiprocessing.Process)` in `_ensure_processes_alive` is never true in practice. Flusher processes are created via `multiprocessing.get_context("spawn").Process`, which produces `multiprocessing.context.SpawnProcess` instances; `SpawnProcess` is a sibling of `multiprocessing.context.Process` (both subclass `multiprocessing.process.BaseProcess`), not a subclass of it, and the only alternative type here is `threading.Thread`, which also fails the check. Consequences: (1) when a flusher process is detected as hung (cause == "hang"), the old process is never killed before `_create_process_for_shards` starts a replacement, so two processes end up flushing the same shards and producing the same segments to the buffered-segments topic (duplicate downstream data), and each restart leaks the previous process's Redis/Kafka connections; the old code called `self.process.kill()` unconditionally, so this is a regression. (2) The identical guard in `join()` (line 346) means `process.terminate()` is also never executed, so flusher processes that outlive the join timeout are not terminated. Use `isinstance(process, multiprocessing.process.BaseProcess)` or invert the check to `not isinstance(process, threading.Thread)`.

findings.title: The added time.sleep(0.1) is a no-op because the test monkeypatches time.sleep
findings.body: Line 15 of this test does `monkeypatch.setattr("time.sleep", lambda _: None)`, so the `time.sleep(0.1)` added at line 62 ("Give flusher threads time to process after drift change") never actually waits. The test therefore depends on the flusher thread being scheduled between `fac._flusher.current_drift.value = 9000` and `step.join()` setting `self.stopped.value = True`; if the thread observes `stopped` before running a flush cycle with the new drift, `messages` stays empty and `(msg,) = messages` fails. This makes the test timing-dependent/flaky. Capture the real sleep before monkeypatching (e.g. `real_sleep = time.sleep` then `real_sleep(0.1)`) or poll until `messages` is non-empty.

findings.title: flusher_processes of 0 or negative is silently mishandled
findings.body: `self.max_processes = max_processes or len(buffer.assigned_shards)` treats an explicit 0 as falsy and turns it into "one process per shard", the opposite of a limit. A negative value (the new `--flusher-processes` click option accepts any int) makes `num_processes = min(max_processes, len(shards))` negative, so `process_to_shards_map` is built as an empty dict and `self.process_to_shards_map[process_index].append(shard)` raises KeyError during consumer startup. Validate that the value is >= 1 (e.g. `click.IntRange(min=1)` on the option in `src/sentry/consumers/__init__.py` and/or an explicit check here).

findings.title: Inconsistent metric tag key: "shards" vs "shard"
findings.body: `spans.buffer.flusher.wait_produce` is emitted with tag key `"shards"`, while `spans.buffer.flusher.produce` (line 185) and `spans.buffer.segment_size_bytes` (line 195) use `"shard"` for the same value. The inconsistent key prevents grouping/comparing these timers under a single tag and looks like a typo.
